evidence: src/business/services/MileageService.ts: constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService) is injected, but averageDaily uses `const prisma = new PrismaClient();`, which bypasses the injected dependency.

src/business/services/MileageService.ts: record uses raw `this.prisma.mileage.create(...)`, while src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts uses the VehicleTable/WorkOrderTable gateways (`this.vehicles.row`, `this.orders.write`).

src/business/services/MileageService.ts: `return km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM;` puts the service-due rule in the service, using a lastServiceKm passed in by the caller, instead of the Vehicle model that owns SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM and lastServiceKm.
src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts: close writes `{ inService: true, ... }` as a literal, while open writes `{ inService: vehicle.inService }`.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two services cover related fleet-maintenance concerns, but MileageService bypasses its own abstractions in two ways. First, MileageService.averageDaily ignores the PrismaService injected in its constructor and creates a new PrismaClient() of its own. That gives it a second, unmanaged connection, so the file does not even use its own dependency consistently. Second, the module has no single persistence abstraction. MaintenanceService works through the domain-oriented table gateways VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable and rebuilds Vehicle and WorkOrder domain objects from them. MileageService goes straight to raw Prisma model access (this.prisma.mileage.create, prisma.mileage.findMany). There is also a likely duplicated rule. MileageService.record computes whether service is due itself (km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM) from a lastServiceKm value the caller passes in, instead of asking the Vehicle domain object, which owns SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM and lastServiceKm. That puts the service-due rule outside the place it belongs. A smaller inconsistency: MaintenanceService.close writes the literal inService: true instead of vehicle.inService, while open writes vehicle.inService.

violations.message: averageDaily creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected PrismaService, which bypasses the module's own injected abstraction.

Uses raw Prisma model access (prisma.mileage.create/findMany), while the sibling MaintenanceService uses domain table gateways (VehicleTable, WorkOrderTable). The module's persistence abstraction is inconsistent.

record computes the service-due rule (`km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM`) from a caller-supplied lastServiceKm instead of delegating to the Vehicle model that owns SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM and lastServiceKm. This duplicates a domain invariant outside its owner.
